findings.passage: But the vigilance has a plain outside cause, and anxiety alone does not make a Six.
findings.problem: The reason given for discounting Type 6 is contradicted by the source the draft itself calls its best test. I opened the June 20, 2020 Dr. K conversation (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=De245b9hRw0, auto-captions, no speaker labels, wording approximate). Before any swatting or the January 2023 deepfake she describes generalized anxiety that was "really severe for like probably around six years" (~00:02), "there's always two thoughts going into everything" and "never any right answer" (~00:06), comfort only in "knowing that there is a plan" (~00:13), asking people "are you mad at me, do you not like me" and then deciding "they lied" (~01:09), "I need reassurance way too much" (~01:10), and "I get confused when people are nice to me" (~01:21). The draft's own trophy story (March 2022) also predates the deepfake, and GQ does not date the swattings. This is more than an emotion: it is doubt of her own judgment, reassurance sought and then disbelieved, and plans used against uncertainty. On this source Type 6 is at least as strong a rival as Type 3, and the draft tests it in three sentences. Type 1 is also set aside in one sentence with no reason given.
findings.acceptance_test: Add the Dr. K recording as an opened source with timestamps and pin every quoted line against the audio. Remove or correct "has a plain outside cause". Give Type 6 a tested case next to Type 3: its best evidence, then a sourced observation that separates it from Type 2, or a plain statement that none does. Give one record-based reason Type 1 trails (for example, her critic is aimed at her productions while her stated stance toward people is permissive). If Type 6 proves the stronger rival, change alternative_type, alternative_case and discriminator in the evidence record plus the description and both type FAQs, and rerun with --refresh --expanded-review. If nothing sourced separates Type 2 from Type 6, hold as insufficient_evidence. Diagnoses and health details are not type evidence; use only what she said and what the argument needs.

findings.passage: "I find my self-worth 100% in 'Oh, she is successful.' And now I'm not that. And so it's like, 'Well, who am I?'"
findings.problem: The Type 3 case rests on this fragment, relayed by Inven Global, and its context changes what it shows. In the same conversation (captions, ~00:12) she does say she was "top in my company" and compares viewer counts, which supports Type 3. But asked where the need to be best came from, she says nobody pressured her: her siblings were varsity athletes, she was cut, and "I just wanted to fit in with my own family" (~01:16). She says of baking "nobody needs a cupcake", that she brings cookies to parties so people are "nicer to me", and agrees "my cookies are my training wheels" (~00:33 to 00:36). She says "I just want them to be happy" and concedes she wants them to like her (~00:29); "I don't want to ask people to care about me" because "it's selfish", and "I don't deserve anyone to care about me", she has to "work hard to earn it" (~00:59); giving others "100" percent happiness returns her "one percent" and "sometimes maybe that's not enough" (~01:03). So she describes achievement as a way to belong and work as how care is earned. That weakens Type 3, changes the reading of the 2025 "work ethic" line, and is the best giving-to-belong evidence in the record. It predates the awards, so it is free of the brand confound the draft worries about. The draft says this recording "is the best single test of the Type 3 reading" and argues the case without it.
findings.acceptance_test: Quote the self-worth line with its surrounding exchange and a timestamp. Add the fit-in, cookies and earn-care passages to the claim inventory as self_report, pinned against audio. Say in the article what they do to the Type 3 case and to "It's the only thing that I've ever found valuable in myself." Label Dr. K's formulations as his (for example that she values herself only with proof of being superior). Weigh her own account that the standard was taught (family, church) against the type explanation, as the standard requires for learned practices, without building a childhood-cause claim. Remove "The full recording was not reviewed" only once it has been.

findings.passage: What she says is missing is not recognition, which she has, but being understood.
findings.problem: The first leg of the discriminator does not separate the types. Both "understood" quotes are about audiences and critics misreading her (Polygon: "on the internet"; BBC: on answering critics). That is a wish for accurate reception, which a Three or anyone clipped out of context shares; the evidence record says so under C21. The draft then treats it as a wish to be known by friends. "Recognition, which she has" also merges two things: admiration for results (GQ, CAA, a million viewers) and appreciation for giving. The draft's best Type 2 evidence is that she says the second is missing ("the dinner I paid for", "I'm not a fucking hero"), so the sentence argues against its own case.
findings.acceptance_test: Restate the leg as admiration for results, which she has and does not cite when hurt, against appreciation and care returned for giving, which she says is missing. Keep the "understood" quotes only with their audience context, outside the discriminator. Bring the FAQ "Why isn't QTCinderella a Type 3?" and the type FAQ into line with the new wording.

findings.passage: This is the center of the Type 2 reading.
findings.problem: The evidence called the center is evidence the draft concedes to the rival two sections later ("a version of me" as a Three's persona), and the research record lists the same claim (C28) as unexplained because distance from peers sits oddly with Type 2. Calling peers coworkers and withholding her surname and birthday is guardedness that a Type 2 reading has to account for. "I so desperately wish I could be understood" and "the rainy cloud in everyone's room" are also not Two-specific; a Type 4 or Type 6 reading claims them as easily. The useful point in the paragraph is the asymmetry (she tracks who will be alone at the table; she says nobody tracks her), and the draft does not say why that favors Type 2.
findings.acceptance_test: Rest the Type 2 case on evidence the rivals do not predict (the 2020 cookies and earn-care statements, the make-up of her complaint lists, low-stakes giving). Present "a version of me" and "coworkers" as shared ground or counterevidence, with the safety reasons the record gives for withholding her name. Either drop the "center" label or add one or two sentences stating what Type 2 predicts here that Type 3 and Type 6 do not.

findings.passage: A person guarding an image does not usually broadcast herself crying against the advice she expects from "everyone in the world," though anyone can break.
findings.problem: A type stereotype is doing the work of evidence. In livestreaming, visible distress is not off-image; it is the medium, and that stream drew sympathy and coverage. A Three could do it, and so could a Six meeting a threat head-on (she vowed to sue in the same stream). The sentence assumes Threes hide feeling, and the same assumption returns in "she does not manage it out of view". The standard asks for one standard across types.
findings.acceptance_test: Remove the generalization about people guarding an image, here and in "The case for Type 3". Keep the fact that she went live expecting to be told not to. Rest this leg on what her two complaint lists contain: in February 2023 and November 2025 she lists what other people received from her and never audience numbers, rank or awards. State that this is the discriminating feature and that both instances come from moments of attack.

findings.passage: Nearly all of the evidence about motive is her own account, given to reporters between 2022 and 2025, often in weeks when she was promoting an event or defending one.
findings.problem: GQ, already opened, holds low-stakes moments seen by the reporter that bear on the discriminator and are missing from the draft and the claim inventory. She asked the reporter to help think of Christmas gifts for her cohosts and mentioned custom keyboard caps she once gave friends that, in GQ's words, she "thinks they went unused". Driving, she pulled over for ambulances "wondering if the person inside is okay" and said "I think I'm empathetic to a fault." She said people treat her like "an LLC", and "I'm not trying to farm sympathy, but there is no sympathy." The keyboard caps are the same bookkeeping as the dinner, in a calm moment, which answers the draft's own worry that both lists come from crises.
findings.acceptance_test: Add at least the gift and ambulance observations, attributed to GQ's reporter, with claims in the inventory. Say what each cannot show (a day with a reporter is still a performance, and empathy is not exclusive to one type).

findings.passage: Her list of failures is about other people: tired guests, a flat last stream, streamers who did not get a turn.
findings.problem: This overreads the quote. Two of her four reasons are about performance ("the last stream wasn't super hype", "I didn't do good enough"), and her next line in Inven Global is "I take it really personally because I just want it to be better." For an event producer the guests' night is the product, so by the draft's own rule that the job cannot separate the two types, this cannot either. Only the people who "didn't get the opportunity to stream" is specifically about inclusion.
findings.acceptance_test: Narrow the claim to the inclusion item and quote or acknowledge "I just want it to be better." Reword the matching sentence in "The case for Type 3" ("her measure of failure was other people's night") so it claims no more than that.

findings.passage: In October 2026 the pattern ran small.
findings.problem: The sentence presents the wedding episode as type evidence without saying which pattern it shows. It was a shared act (Ahgren said the harsher line), the audio was not reviewed, and the research notes say the companion Ludwig Ahgren draft uses the same wedding as evidence for Type 7. Her own remark is a planner's complaint about lost photos, which fits several types.
findings.acceptance_test: Either name the pattern and show what in her own words makes it specific to the leading type, or report the episode as record with no pattern claim. Check that the Ludwig Ahgren page does not cite the same act as proof of a different type without a person-specific reason.

protected_passages.passage: Both are things a host does. One finds the guest who knows nobody a kind neighbor. The other reads the bill out loud.
protected_passages.reason: States the whole type question (attention to who is alone, and a ledger when hurt) from two sourced acts, with no type vocabulary. It holds whichever rival the edit ends up testing.

protected_passages.passage: Running an awards show pays in gratitude and in status at once, so the job cannot separate the two.
protected_passages.reason: The correct method statement: it rules out the career itself as type evidence and forces the argument onto narrower observations.

protected_passages.passage: A stated mission is also a brand. The girl nobody came to see who now throws the party is a very good origin story for an events business, and she may tell it because it works.
protected_passages.reason: Names the professional-incentive explanation for her own best Type 2 story instead of taking it at face value.

protected_passages.passage: She wants the effort seen and disowns the wish in the same sentence.
protected_passages.reason: A precise, quote-bound reading of a motive at work. This is the kind of observation the discriminator should be built from.

protected_passages.passage: Keeping "my thing" is a claim of ownership. Choosing Higa is a gift. A Two or a Three could have made that call.
protected_passages.reason: Admits that a vivid anecdote does not discriminate. Keeps the reader's trust for the places where the draft does claim a difference.

assessment: The Type 2 read is plausible and the draft is honest about its limits, with no wings or arrows used as patches. The argument as written does not yet beat its alternatives. Two of the three discriminator legs fail on inspection: "understood" is about audience reception, and the crying-on-stream point rests on a stereotype of Type 3. The third leg (when hurt, she lists what others got from her, never numbers or rank) is real and specific and should carry more weight. The larger problem is the source the draft names as its best test and did not open. I opened the 2020 Dr. K conversation through its auto-captions. It cuts two ways. It strengthens Type 2 against Type 3: she describes achievement as a way to fit in, cookies as how she gets people to be nicer to her, and care as something she must earn and should not ask for. It also shows years of doubt, reassurance-seeking and distrust of kindness before the events the draft uses to explain her vigilance, so Type 6 is a serious rival that the draft dismisses on a wrong timeline. Type 3 may not be the strongest alternative. I did not flag major_thesis_change because the frozen draft makes none; if the edit changes the alternative type or the leading type, that needs --refresh --expanded-review. sensitive_allegations stays flagged: the Dr. K source adds personal health and family disclosures that the edit must handle with restraint. Sources reopened in this review: GQ (full), Inven Global (full), Dr. K captions (full; quotes are approximate and need audio pinning; the repo should get fragments and timestamps only). Polygon could not be reopened (fetch blocked), so C20 and C21 wording is unverified here. Similarity: the diagnostic tripped on two lines against the Olivia Dean draft, the not-a-diagnosis sentence and a one-line gloss of Type 2 ("the giving goes unseen"). Both are ordinary type vocabulary. The matched argument excerpts differ in substance, so I raise no reuse finding. I compared only the excerpts in the diagnostic, not the other drafts in full.
